readings.core: At fixed batch size, more robots shorten trajectories: training accelerates, but excessive parallelism lowers reward, attributed to inadequate temporal information. Throughput saturation and larger batches' reward-versus-time cost support a bounded reward-time balance rather than unlimited scaling.
readings.scope: The comparison uses reduced stair/obstacle heights, no curriculum, five runs, and rewards after 1,500 updates. The suggested balance is 2,048-4,096 robots and 100,000-200,000 samples; the 20,000-robot baseline has a different sample budget.

readings.core: GPU-local simulation, collection, and PPO reduce transfers; relocating robots adapts difficulty without regenerating terrain. Adequate rollout lengths constrain parallelism. Reported training time and physical traversal support rapid training and hardware deployment, while imperfect terrain maps reduce robustness and prompt a speed cap.
readings.scope: The run uses 4,096 ANYmal C robots, 98,304 samples per batch, 1,500 updates, and an RTX A6000: under 20 minutes. Simulation stair success concerns crossings without base contact up to 0.2 m; uphill traversal fails beyond 25 degrees. Hardware commands are limited to 0.6 m/s.
readings.core_witness: Keeping simulation, data collection, and proximal policy optimization (PPO) on one GPU reduces CPU-GPU transfers.

readings.core: Time limits interrupt continuing trajectories without observable episode time, so the critic cannot anticipate them. Treating these resets as terminal would discard continuation value. Separating time-outs and adding the critic's discounted future-return prediction preserves that value for the interrupted trajectory, not the newly reset episode.
readings.scope: This distinction concerns time-outs versus failure or goal completion. The 20-second limit is independent of rollout length; updates do not reset environments, so episodes span batches and time-outs need not occur only at a batch's final step.
readings.core_witness: augments their rewards with the critic's discounted prediction of future return
readings.scope_witness: the 20-second episode limit is independent of the number of steps collected per policy update

readings.core: Unlike predictable task endings, time limits interrupt continuing trajectories without observable episode time. Treating them as terminal discards predicted future return. Reporting time-outs separately and augmenting their reward with the critic's discounted remaining-return estimate keeps continuation value in the target instead of equating reset with completion.
readings.scope: The distinction is between failure/goal completion and time-limit resets. Episodes last up to 20 seconds and span multiple short batches; policy updates do not reset environments, so time-outs may occur within a batch rather than only at its final step.
